claims.claim: the Whitledge et al. (2003) smallmouth set's respiration was measured only at 18–30 °C, on Missouri fish (via Brownscombe, Smith & Bzonek 2024)
claims.quote: from Missouri, United States, including metabolic rate and growth scope from 18 to 30
claims.conditions: 'Whitledge et al. (2002, 2003) examined smallmouth bass from Missouri, United States, including metabolic rate and growth scope from 18 to 30 °C'; elsewhere: the FB4 smallmouth metabolism component 'is parameterized from lab-based estimates of their RMR from smaller-bodied individuals (Deslauriers et al., 2017; Whitledge et al., 2002)'
claims.note: Brownscombe credits the respirometry to Whitledge et al. 2002 (subadult, 'smaller-bodied' fish) and the model to 2003; say 'the set's respiration (Whitledge et al. 2002) was measured on smaller-bodied Missouri fish at 18–30 °C'. 'Only' is the paper's gloss, consistent with the source.

claims.claim: swim-tunnel resting metabolism of a 1-kg smallmouth extrapolates to 61–78 mg O₂ kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ at 2–8 °C (Brownscombe, Smith & Bzonek 2024; extrapolation by the project)
claims.location: p. 257 (PDF p. 4), Table 2, model 'ln (MO2) = speed + ln (mass) + temperature + speed × temperature + sex' (page image checked); method p. 256 (PDF p. 3)
claims.conditions: RMR is the speed–MO2 model evaluated at zero swimming speed ('The swimming speed–MO2 model was used to predict smallmouth bass resting metabolic rate (RMR), when swimming speed was zero'), not a measured resting rate. Fish 0.67–2.05 kg from the lower Otonabee River, Ontario, tested at 6, 12, 18 and 24 °C after ≥ 5 d acclimation; 2 °C is below the measured range (the authors extrapolated to 1–35 °C themselves). Females add 0.01 to ln MO2
claims.note: Redone for a 1-kg male (ln mass = 0, speed 0): exp(4.04 + 0.04 × 2) = 61.6 and exp(4.04 + 0.04 × 8) = 78.3 mg O₂ kg⁻¹ h⁻¹ (female 62.2–79.0). The coefficients are printed to two decimals only (temperature 0.04, SE 0.002), so 0.035–0.045 °C⁻¹ would give 61–75 to 62–82; the range is good to about ±5 %. The table's model heading names a 'speed × temperature' term but its row reads 'Speed × ln (mass)' (−0.002, p = 0.53); neither matters at zero speed.

notes: Both uses check. Relevant context the paper may want: the authors themselves expect smallmouth bass 'become largely dormant in winter months in the north-temperate regions', with very limited aerobic scope below 5 °C, and expect small fish to be most constrained in winter (pp. 259–260, PDF pp. 6–7) — note beside §3.5.4's 'quiescent rather than dormant' (Suski & Ridgway 2009). Other values: all measured MO2 197 ± 58 (61–332) mg O₂ kg⁻¹ h⁻¹; mean measured MO2 at 6 °C 85 ± 14 (61–102), all while swimming (Table 1); MMR peaks at an estimated 22 °C; aerobic scope peaks at 20 °C, > 90 % at 17–24 °C, > 50 % at 11–28 °C, falling to zero at 3 and 32 °C; Ucrit 58 cm/s at 6 °C to 93 cm/s at 24 °C (pp. 257–258). The project's 'about 60 % of body energy in 150 days' is not from this source and was not checked here.
